[1] The event ran from October 1 to October 14, 2023, with some shelters extending the event to October 15. [1, 4, 6] A total of 360 shelters across 43 states participated, offering reduced adoption fees of $50 or less to encourage adoptions and alleviate overcrowding in shelters. [1] The initiative led to 10,795 cats and 9,841 dogs finding new homes. [1] Announcements promoting the event were made in late September 2023, highlighting the crisis of overcrowding in the nation's animal shelters due to increased owner surrenders and stray intakes. [4, 7] <4> To combat the nationwide shelter overcrowding crisis, the BISSELL Pet Foundation hosted its Fall National 'Empty the Shelters' event from October 1 to 15, 2023. [1] The event, which was announced on September 20, 2023, involved over 345 animal welfare organizations across 42 states. [1] During the event, the foundation sponsored reduced adoption fees, allowing adopters to take home a fully vaccinated, microchipped, and spayed or neutered pet for $50 or less. [1] Cathy Bissell, the founder of the foundation, highlighted the severe overcrowding in shelters, stating that the event aimed to save lives by creating space for more animals in need. [1] <5> Best Friends Animal Society hosted its sixth National Adoption Weekend from September 15-17, 2023, to address overcrowding in animal shelters. [1, 2, 3] In collaboration with over 680 local shelters and rescue organizations across the United States, the event featured waived or reduced adoption fees for cats and dogs. [1, 4] This initiative aimed to save the lives of shelter pets by encouraging community members to adopt, thereby freeing up space for other animals in need. [1, 4] All adopted pets were spayed or neutered, vaccinated, and microchipped before going to their new homes. [1] <6> In a roundtable discussion reported on August 23, 2023, data concerning the first half of 2023 was presented by Stephanie Filer of Shelter Animals Count, Melissa Thibault of the ASPCA, and April Hunstman of Adopt a Pet. [2, 4] For existing pet stores, the law mandates a five-year phase-out period to cease the sale of dogs, cats, and rabbits sourced from commercial breeders. Recent related events (events are separated by numbered tags): <1> In 2025, animal shelters across the United States are facing an unprecedented crisis due to a significant increase in pet surrenders. [1, 2, 5, 8] This nationwide trend, reported in cities like Chicago, Philadelphia, San Diego, and across Wisconsin, is primarily driven by economic hardships affecting pet owners. [2, 4, 6, 8, 9] Factors include the rising costs of veterinary care and pet food, housing insecurity such as evictions, and additional pet fees charged by landlords. [4, 6, 9] For instance, a Philadelphia shelter reported that nearly 40% of surrenders in 2025 were due to such financial and housing difficulties, while Chicago has seen a staggering 237% increase in dog surrenders since 2019. [4, 9] This influx has led to severe overcrowding, with many shelters operating well over capacity, creating waitlists for the first time, and having to halve kennel spaces to accommodate more animals. [2, 3, 5, 7, 8, 9] In response, shelters and animal welfare organizations have intensified their efforts by implementing various outreach programs and adoption initiatives. These include pleas for foster homes and donations, offering pet food assistance, providing resources for veterinary care, organizing adoption events with reduced fees, and establishing temporary housing for pets of owners in crisis. [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 7, 8, 9] <2> A bill to enhance the standard of care for animals in New York shelters was introduced in the State Legislature. The Assembly version, A8555, was introduced by Assemblymember Paulin on May 20, 2025, and its companion, Senate Bill S8211, was introduced by Senator Addabbo on May 21, 2025. [3, 4, 6] Both bills were referred to their respective Committees on Agriculture. [3, 4] The legislation aims to clarify care standards for animals housed in or being transported by shelters.
